narrative.overview:
Qaboom is read by a reviewer who lives in it for hours and a manager who opens it to answer one question — is this defensible? The system behaves like instrumentation rather than a brochure: flat, dense, hairline-ruled, nothing decorated that could instead be measured.

The register is the call-intelligence category executed at full fidelity — a deliberate commitment, because the product needs to read as a peer of the tools a buyer already evaluates. Distinctiveness lives in the graded call itself, where a speaker timeline, evidence markers and a synced transcript turn a verdict into something you can hear.

Colour is rationed hard. The interface is near-neutral so green, red and oxblood mean exactly one thing each. Brand indigo is an action colour, never a mood. Indigo and teal are reserved as data — they identify speakers, nothing else.
keyCharacteristics: Flat by default; hairlines and tonal steps carry structure, not shadows
Dense over airy — more rows visible beats more whitespace
Tabular figures everywhere a number can be compared
Semantic colour reserved for verdicts; brand colour reserved for action
Speaker colour is information, not ornament
Every text tier clears WCAG AA; one tier is explicitly non-text

rules.name: The Verdict Monopoly Rule
rules.body: Green, red and oxblood mean pass, fail and auto-fail. Nothing else on any screen may use them.

rules.name: The Non-Text Floor Rule
rules.body: decor (#94a3b8) is 2.6:1 and may never carry text. When a value looks too light, take the next tier up, never a new lighter value.

rules.name: The Speaker Colour Rule
rules.body: Indigo and teal identify speakers. A surface not about who was talking does not use them as accents.

rules.name: The Five Steps Rule
rules.body: 28 / 24 / 18 / 14 / 12px, and no others. 24px exists solely for metric readouts. A value that feels like it needs 16px, 20px or 13px is a weight or colour problem, not a missing size.

rules.name: The Tight Floor Rule
rules.body: The 14 to 12px step is 1.17x on purpose. Below body, weight, case and colour carry the distinction instead of size.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any figure a user might compare down a column gets tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Earned Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow requires a real z-relationship. Decorative elevation on a resting panel is a defect.

rules.name: The Three Radii Rule
rules.body: 6px contains, 4px controls, 2px marks. The 2px tier is only available to elements under 8px tall; anything larger takes 4px. A fourth value is drift.

dos: Do reach for a hairline and a tonal step before reaching for a shadow.
Do give every number a comparison job tabular-nums.
Do put evidence and guidance in the 58ch citation treatment, under the thing they qualify.
Do label every form control visibly; placeholders disappear on first keystroke.
Do keep the verdict vocabulary to pass / fail / critical, and render critical as the only solid fill.
Do let a surface render honestly when data is missing.
donts: Don't use a colour below 4.5:1 for text. decor exists for glyphs only.
Don't add a sixth type size or a 13px tier.
Don't put green, red or oxblood on anything that is not a verdict.
Don't use speaker indigo or teal as a general accent.
Don't put a thick coloured border on the side or top of a card.
Don't render a chart, waveform or ratio from data the product does not actually have.
Don't introduce a radius between the three steps, or above 6px on a panel.
